definition_title: Binary column codes, one-sided expansion and finite probabilities
natural_language_statement:
A binary generator is an $m\times n$ matrix $G$ over $\mathbb F_2$; its code consists of all column products $Gx$. No column-independence assumption is made. A word's weight is the number of its nonzero coordinates. For a row set $S$, let $\Gamma_G(S)$ be the columns touched by those rows. The matrix is $(\gamma,k,t)$-expanding when every row has weight exactly $k$ and
$$|\Gamma_G(S)|\ge\gamma k|S|\quad\text{for every }|S|\le t.$$
The empty row set is included. Finite event probabilities sum the masses of the outcomes in the event. Uniform probability uses the uniform law on a nonempty finite type. For binary words of length $m$, the mass of an independent Bernoulli-$p$ word $e$ is $p^{|\operatorname{supp}(e)|}(1-p)^{m-|\operatorname{supp}(e)|}$.

These conventions supply the generator, graph and noise interface used throughout the mission. The published neighborhood and isolated left-expansion predicates are reused without their surrounding quantum-code assumptions.

**Formalization Note** Indices start at zero. The published normalized row cutoff is $t/m$ when $m>0$; an empty row type has a vacuous expansion condition and row-weight condition. All theorem-level construction assertions hold eventually with $m>n\ge2$. Bernoulli masses are used only at valid probabilities.
definition:
import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_QuantumExpander_Decoder_Setting
set_option autoImplicit false
open scoped Classical

namespace ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch

open scoped BigOperators
abbrev Bit := ZMod 2
abbrev Word (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bit
abbrev Generator (m n : ℕ) := Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Bit
noncomputable def weight {I K : Type*} [Fintype I] [Zero K] (v : I → K) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter fun i => v i ≠ 0).card
noncomputable def neighbors {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (G : Matrix I J Bit) (S : Finset I) : Finset J := by
  classical
  exact QuantumExpander.Decoder.nbhdA (fun i j => G i j ≠ 0) S
noncomputable def RowWeight {I J : Type*} [Fintype J] (G : Matrix I J Bit) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, weight (G i) = k
noncomputable def Expanding {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (G : Matrix I J Bit) (γ : ℝ) (k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : Prop := by
  classical
  exact RowWeight G k ∧
    (if Fintype.card I = 0 then True else
      QuantumExpander.Decoder.IsLeftExpanding (fun i j => G i j ≠ 0) k
        (t / Fintype.card I) (1 - γ))
noncomputable def eventProb {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] (P : PMF Ω) (E : Ω → Prop) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ ω, if E ω then (P ω).toReal else 0
noncomputable def uniformProb {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (E : Ω → Prop) : ℝ :=
  eventProb (PMF.uniformOfFintype Ω) E
noncomputable def bernoulliWord (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (v : Word m) : ℝ :=
  p ^ weight v * (1 - p) ^ (m - weight v)

end ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch
source: Isaac M Hair, Amit Sahai, Expanding Codes with Polynomial Stretch, STOC 2027 submission #824 (October 2026), printed p. 1 / PDF p. 2, §1, generator and expansion definitions; printed p. 2 / PDF p. 3, Bernoulli convention.
